what_it_does: Training a large AI model requires splitting the work across many machines simultaneously — some machines handle different slices of the input data (data parallelism), others hold different parts of the model's weight tables (model or tensor parallelism), and yet others split the optimizer's bookkeeping (optimizer sharding). Combining these strategies is powerful but tricky: the code quickly becomes tangled, and it is hard to verify that the parallelism is correct or to try different combinations without rewriting large parts of the implementation. PartIR provides a clean API where each parallelization strategy is expressed as a simple, declarative transformation that rewrites the model's internal computation graph (its intermediate representation) step by step. Because each transformation follows well-defined rules and the result can be inspected after every step, engineers and automated tools can reason about and verify the combined strategy incrementally, independently of the specific hardware or runtime being used.
